how-much-does-kickstarter-take.html.text:
← Kickstarter fee calculator

How much does Kickstarter take?

Kickstarter charges two fees, and only if a campaign meets its funding goal: a flat 5% platform fee on the total raised, plus a per-pledge processing fee that is charged once per pledge, not once per dollar — and the processing rate itself changes below a $10 pledge. A flat “8-10%” summary misses both of those, and can be wrong in either direction.

Worked example 1: a $50 pledge

LineAmount
Pledge amount$50.00
Platform fee (5%)$2.50
Processing fee (3% + $0.20)$1.70
Total fee$4.20
Creator keeps$45.80 (91.6%)

Worked example 2: a $5 micro-pledge pays a higher rate

Pledges under $10 fall into the micro-pledge processing tier — 5% + $0.05 instead of 3% + $0.20 — on top of the same 5% platform fee.

LineAmount
Pledge amount$5.00
Platform fee (5%)$0.25
Processing fee, micro tier (5% + $0.05)$0.30
Total fee$0.55
Creator keeps$4.45 (89%)

89% kept versus 91.6% on the $50 example — a smaller pledge pays a higher effective rate, because the flat $0.05 (or $0.20) processing charge is a bigger share of a smaller number, and the percentage itself is higher below $10.

Worked example 3: more backers, same raise, less kept

The per-pledge flat charge means a campaign's effective rate depends on how many pledges it took to reach the total, not just the total itself.

CampaignTotal raisedBackersAvg. pledgeTotal feeEffective rate
A$10,000500$20.00$9009%
B$10,0001,000$10.00$1,00010%

Same $10,000 raised. Campaign B's fee is $100 higher, purely because twice as many pledges means twice as many flat per-pledge processing charges spread across the same total.

Do this with your own numbers

The Kickstarter fee calculator runs this same arithmetic on a single pledge or a whole campaign's totals, flags which processing tier applies, and shows the effective rate. Nothing you type leaves your browser.

Common questions

How much does Kickstarter take on a $50 pledge?

A 5% platform fee ($2.50) plus a standard-tier processing fee of 3% + $0.20 ($1.70), for a total fee of $4.20 -- the creator keeps $45.80, or 91.6% of the pledge.

Why does a $5 pledge pay a higher rate than a $50 pledge?

Pledges under $10 fall into Kickstarter's micro-pledge processing tier: 5% + $0.05, instead of the standard 3% + $0.20. On a $5 pledge that is a $0.25 platform fee plus a $0.30 processing fee, $0.55 total -- 11% of the pledge, versus 8.4% on the $50 example. The flat per-pledge component is a bigger share of a smaller pledge, and the percentage itself is higher below $10.

Does a campaign keep less if it has more backers, even raising the same total?

Yes. A $10,000 campaign funded by 500 backers (a $20 average pledge) pays about $900 in total fees, a 9% effective rate. The same $10,000 funded by 1,000 backers (a $10 average pledge) pays about $1,000, a 10% effective rate -- $100 more, from the same raise, because the flat per-pledge processing charge is spread across twice as many transactions.

      Common questions

      How much does Kickstarter take from a funded project?

      On Kickstarter's published US schedule: a 5% platform fee on the total amount pledged, plus payment processing charged per pledge — 3% of the pledge plus $0.20 for pledges of $10 or more, or 5% plus $0.05 for pledges under $10. Combined, most US campaigns land around 8-10% of the total raise, and fees are charged only if the project is funded.

      Why do two campaigns with the same total raised pay different fees?

      Because the processing fee's $0.20 (or $0.05) component is charged once per pledge, not once per dollar. A campaign that raises $10,000 from 100 backers averaging $100 each pays that flat charge 100 times; the same $10,000 from 1,000 backers averaging $10 each pays it 1,000 times. More, smaller pledges keep a smaller share of an identical total raised — reward-tier pricing changes the fee, not just the marketing.

      What happens if the project does not reach its funding goal?

      Nothing is charged. Kickstarter is all-or-nothing: no pledge is collected and no fee applies unless the funding goal is met by the deadline.

      Is my data uploaded anywhere?

      No. Parsing and arithmetic happen entirely in your browser. The total raised, backer count, and any pledge amount you enter are never uploaded. The optional usage counter records only which features were used and the day, never any of your numbers.

vs-the-flat-8-10-percent-rule-of-thumb.h.text:
← Kickstarter Fee Calculator

This calculator vs. the flat “8-10%” rule of thumb

“Kickstarter takes 8-10%” is the number every guide repeats. It is also a single percentage applied to the whole raise, with no line for how many backers it came from — which is exactly what changes the real number.

What each approach actually involves

The flat rule of thumb takes one number from the 8-10% range and multiplies the whole campaign total by it. One number, one multiplication, done — and the same guess for a campaign funded by 150 backers or by 1,250.

This calculator prices Kickstarter's two real fees separately: a 5% platform fee on the total, and a per-pledge processing fee that is 3% + $0.20 for pledges of $10 or more, or 5% + $0.05 for pledges under $10. Because the flat component is charged per pledge, not per dollar, the calculator asks for the total raised and the number of backers, so the average pledge size — and its effect on the real rate — is part of the answer instead of invisible.

$10,000 raised, by backer countFlat 9% guess (the “8-10%” midpoint)This calculator (priced separately)
150 backers, $66.67 average pledge (this calculator's shipped default)$9,100.00 net — $900.00 fee$9,170.00 net — $830.00 fee (8.30% effective)
1,250 backers, $8.00 average pledge (micro-pledge tier)$9,100.00 net — $900.00 fee$8,937.50 net — $1,062.50 fee (10.625% effective)

Same $10,000 raised, same flat 9% guess both times. Against the 150-backer campaign the guess overstates the fee by $70.00. Against the 1,250-backer campaign — same total, smaller average pledge — the identical guess understates the fee by $162.50, and the real effective rate, 10.625%, is past the top of the “8-10%” range most guides quote. A single flat number cannot be wrong in only one direction here; which way it misses depends on a figure it never asked for.

This tool needs no account and no sign-in: it is a static page, the arithmetic runs in your browser, and once it has loaded it keeps working with the connection off.

Common questions

What is the flat “8-10%” rule of thumb this page compares against?

Picking one number in the 8-10% range that guides quote for Kickstarter's combined fees, and multiplying the whole campaign total by it. It is a one-line estimate that treats the fee as a flat percentage of the raise, with no line for how many backers it came from.

How much can the flat rule of thumb get a real campaign wrong?

On this calculator's own default example -- a $10,000 campaign -- a flat 9% guess (the midpoint of “8-10%”) prices the fee at $900.00 and the net payout at $9,100.00 no matter how many backers it came from. At the calculator's shipped default of 150 backers ($66.67 average pledge), the real fee is $830.00 and the real net payout is $9,170.00 -- the guess overstated the fee by $70.00. Spread across 1,250 backers instead ($8.00 average pledge, the micro-pledge tier), the real fee is $1,062.50 and the real net payout is $8,937.50 -- the same guess now understated the fee by $162.50. Same $10,000 raised, same flat guess, a $232.50 swing in which direction it is wrong.

Why does average pledge size change the effective rate at all?

Because Kickstarter's payment-processing fee has a flat per-pledge component ($0.20, or $0.05 under $10) on top of its percentage -- charged once per pledge, not once per dollar. More, smaller pledges spread that flat charge across more transactions, so the same total raised pays more in processing the more backers it took to raise it. A flat percentage guess has no way to see that, because it only ever looks at the total.

Does the real rate ever fall outside the quoted “8-10%” range entirely?

Yes. The calculator's own micro-pledge example above -- 1,250 backers averaging $8.00 each -- lands at a 10.625% effective rate, past the top of the range most summaries quote. A campaign built on very small pledges is not a rare edge case for something like a sticker tier or a $5 digital thank-you, and “8-10%” undersells its real cost.

Does this page assert Kickstarter's current fee schedule?

The 5% platform fee and the per-pledge processing rates (3% + $0.20 standard, 5% + $0.05 under $10) are constants lifted from Kickstarter's own published US fee schedule, not a live fetch. Confirm the current schedule at kickstarter.com/help/fees before relying on either this calculator or any rule of thumb for a real campaign.
